QF.id: AIF Valuation Taxation and Good Practices_7

question.text: The main challenge in valuing illiquid AIF investments is:

answer.text: Illiquidity, lack of an organized market or observable data, and reliance on judgemental assumptions

explanation.text: The Logic: The XIX-A workbook describes valuation of illiquid AIF investments as complex because there is no organized market or readily observable price data, valuation is judgemental and assumption-heavy, and observable market inputs (where available) are less subjective than valuer assumptions. The Trap: Having too many data points or too much liquidity is the opposite of the actual challenge; there is no prohibition on valuation by regulators. Note: The wording is tied to the workbook's terms (illiquidity, lack of observable data, judgemental assumptions) rather than broad "market-determined prices" phrasing.
